summary: Describes using ATM Adaptation Layer 5 (AAL5) to frame PPP-encapsulated packets, so PPP can run directly over ATM.

eli5.summary: A way to wrap internet data in small cells so it can ride on an ATM network.

questions: how does ppp run over atm
subtitle: How to run PPP directly over an ATM virtual connection, using AAL5 frames in place of HDLC framing.

tldr.problem: PPP normally uses HDLC-like framing, but on an ATM network with point-to-point connections there is a ready-made framing layer, AAL5, that PPP could use instead.
tldr.mechanism: A PPP frame becomes the payload of an AAL5 CPCS-PDU, either bare on its own virtual circuit (VC-multiplexed) or behind a small LLC header and NLPID value of 0xCF (LLC encapsulated). Implementations MUST support both.
tldr.outcome: PPP keeps its LCP, NCP, authentication and compression features over ATM, with a few LCP options forbidden and rules for handling unexpected switches between the two encapsulations.

today: RFC 2364 is a Proposed Standard from July 1998, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 1661 for PPP and RFC 1483 for AAL5 encapsulation.

sections.title: Why PPP Over AAL5
sections.content:
ATM AAL5 provides virtual connections between end stations on the same network. These connections offer a packet delivery service that includes error detection but no error correction. Most existing implementations of PPP use ISO 3309 HDLC as the basis for framing, but when an ATM network is configured with point-to-point connections, PPP can use AAL5 as its framing mechanism instead.

The RFC is aimed at implementations that want PPP facilities such as the Link Control Protocol, Network-layer Control Protocols, authentication and compression. These need a point-to-point relationship between the peers and are not designed for the multi-point relationships available in ATM and other multi-access environments.
sections.eli5: PPP needs a way to wrap its messages. ATM already has a wrapping system, so PPP can just borrow it, as long as there are only two ends talking.

sections.title: What PPP Expects From AAL5
sections.content:
PPP treats the AAL5 layer as a bit-synchronous point-to-point link, and one PPP link corresponds to one AAL5 virtual connection. That connection MUST be full-duplex and point to point. It MAY be dedicated (permanent, set up by provisioning) or switched (set up on demand).

The boundary between PPP and AAL5 has three requirements. It is an octet interface, with no provision for sub-octets. PPP imposes no limit on transmission rate or ATM traffic descriptor parameters. AAL5 MUST supply control signals saying when the virtual connection is connected or disconnected; these become the Up and Down events for the LCP state machine.
sections.eli5: PPP needs a two-way pipe between exactly two ends, measured in whole bytes, and it needs to be told when the pipe opens or closes.

sections.title: The Two Encapsulations
sections.content:
The RFC reuses the frame structure of the multiprotocol encapsulation over AAL5 (RFC 1483), which defines two ways to identify the payload type: virtual circuit based multiplexing, where both ends agree on the type for the whole circuit, and LLC encapsulation, where each PDU carries an in-band LLC header. An implementation MUST support both for PPP.

In an AAL5 CPCS-PDU, the payload holds up to 2^16 - 1 octets, followed by a PAD of 0 to 47 octets and a trailer of CPCS-UU (1 octet), CPI (1 octet, coded 0x00 when only alignment is used), Length (2 octets) and CRC (4 octets). A Length of 0x00 is used for the abort function.

With VC-multiplexed PPP, the PPP frame (protocol ID of 8 or 16 bits, information and padding, as defined in RFC 1661) is the whole CPCS-PDU payload. With LLC encapsulated PPP, the payload starts with an LLC header of destination SAP 0xFE, source SAP 0xFE and UI frame type 0x03, then the NLPID for PPP, 0xCF, then the PPP protocol identifier (1 or 2 octets) and the information field.

Endpoints MAY be provisioned to carry other LLC-encapsulated protocols on the same circuit, but MUST NOT send packets of any protocol that has an active NCP in the PPP session.
sections.eli5: There are two ways to label the package. Either the whole road is agreed to carry only PPP, or every package carries a little sticker saying it is PPP.

sections.title: Choosing an Encapsulation on Switched Circuits
sections.content:
For permanent circuits both ends are configured to agree. For a switched circuit, the implementation MUST negotiate with the Q.2931 Annex C procedure, using the Broadband Lower Layer Interface (B-LLI) information element. The caller MUST request VC-multiplexed PPP, LLC-encapsulated PPP, or both in the SETUP message. When both are offered, the two B-LLI elements are listed in order of preference inside a Broadband Repeat Indicator element.

The called side MUST be able to accept a call offering LLC-encapsulated PPP, and MUST reject a call that offers only an encapsulation it does not support. A caller offering both MUST be able to negotiate LLC-encapsulated PPP.

For VC-multiplexed calls, the layer 3 protocol field selects ISO/IEC TR 9577 and the extension octets give an IPI value of PPP (0xCF). For LLC calls, the layer 2 protocol field selects LAN Logical Link Control (ISO/IEC8802-2). One exception: a Frame Relay/ATM FRF.8 interworking unit connecting to an RFC 1973 end point MUST use LLC encapsulated PPP, and is exempt from supporting VC-multiplexed PPP.
sections.eli5: When a call is placed on demand, the caller says which labeling style it wants, maybe giving a first and second choice, and the other side can say no if it does not know the style.

sections.title: Unexpected Encapsulation Changes
sections.content:
If a virtual connection loses state, the peer may change encapsulation without warning, from VC-multiplexed to LLC encapsulated or the reverse. To spot this, the RFC notes what LCP packets look like. With LLC encapsulation the first 6 octets of the AAL5 frame are fe-fe-03-cf-c0-21. With VC-multiplexing the frame starts with just c0-21 (2 octets).

If, after a PPP link has reached the Network-layer Protocol phase and negotiated an NCP, a frame arrives in the other equivalent encapsulation, the link MUST react. On a switched circuit it MUST immediately clear the call with cause value 111, protocol error, unspecified. On a permanent circuit it MUST tear down the active NCPs, SHOULD generate an error message, enter the Termination state and silently drop all received packets. The purpose is to prevent black holes when a peer loses state.
sections.eli5: If one side suddenly switches to the other labeling style, the other side notices from the first few bytes, hangs up, and starts over rather than silently losing messages.

sections.title: LCP Option Rules
sections.content:
The Magic Number LCP option is RECOMMENDED and the Protocol Field Compression option is NOT RECOMMENDED. An implementation MUST NOT request, and MUST reject a request for, the Field Check Sequence alternatives, Address-and-Control-Field-Compression, or the Asynchronous-Control-Character-Map. The first and last of these relate to HDLC-style framing, which AAL5 replaces with its own trailer.

The Maximum-Receive-Unit option MUST NOT be negotiated larger than the maximum CPCS-SDU size for the virtual connection in that direction. Where a PPP link is bridged over several AAL5 sections, each section's LCP framing options MUST be negotiated independently by the bridging converters. For a permanent circuit in the Stopped state, the RFC recommends waiting for Configure-Requests.
sections.eli5: Some of the usual PPP settings only make sense for old-style lines, so here they are banned. The biggest message size is capped by what the ATM connection allows.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC argues that ATM networks are generally virtual circuit based, so security is implicit in the provider's administration of Permanent Virtual Circuits, and the chance of a breach from mis-routed cells is considered negligible. With Switched Virtual Circuits, the model resembles dial-up modem access, and the same PAP and CHAP authentication used for Internet dial-up applies, giving security at parity with those practices.

Applications needing stronger security are encouraged to use authentication headers, encrypted payloads, or ATM-layer security. With LLC encapsulation, an end point cannot assume that PPP session authentication also protects other LLC-encapsulated flows on the same virtual connection.
sections.eli5: A private line is hard to tap, and logging in works as it does for dial-up. For secrets, add more locks. Other traffic sharing the line is not covered by the PPP login.
